title: Unity of Scripture
definition: The Unity of Scripture means the Bible’s many books form one consistent, God-given message centered on His redemptive work in Christ.
summary: The Unity of Scripture means the Bible’s many books form one consistent, God-given message centered on His redemptive work in Christ.
christFocus: Jesus brings the unity of Scripture into focus because the promises, patterns, commands, warnings, and hopes of the Bible find their fulfillment in Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Bible contains many books, authors, genres, and historical settings, yet it tells one unified story under God’s authorship. That unity is not forced by human imagination; it rests on God’s faithful purpose.

The unity of Scripture helps believers read individual passages without losing the larger story. Creation, fall, promise, covenant, redemption, Church, mission, judgment, and new creation all belong to one unfolding plan.

Christ is the center of that unity. The Scriptures lead to Him, bear witness to Him, and show the fullness of God’s purpose in Him. Unity does not flatten the Bible; it reveals the harmony of God’s redemptive work.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people feel overwhelmed by the Bible because it seems like disconnected stories and teachings. The unity of Scripture helps them see that God is not scattered or confused; He is faithfully revealing one saving plan.

This doctrine also protects against pitting one part of Scripture against another. God’s Word is diverse in form but united in truth.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Read each passage carefully while remembering the whole story of Scripture. Ask how the text fits God’s redemptive plan, how it relates to Christ, and how it calls you to trust and obey the same faithful God.
